title: Local kernel-power membership kills low coefficients
statement: Let A be a commutative ring, d,n natural numbers, B=A[[X_1,...,X_d]], z:Spec A to Spec B the constant-coefficient zero section, and V any open in Spec B. Write r:B to Gamma(V,O) for canonical restriction. For each x in z^{-1}(V), if the germ of r(b) belongs to the nth power of the kernel of the restricted zero-section stalk map, then every coefficient of b of total degree less than n has zero germ in the base stalk at x. Neither depth nor Noetherianity is required.

proof.text: Use the canonical spectrum-stalk and open-restriction isomorphisms to identify the stalk arrow with the localization of constant coefficient. Naturality of the canonical affine section isomorphism and germ restriction identifies the germ of the restricted series with b/1.

Coefficientwise localization to A_p[[X]] makes every denominator outside the zero-section prime invertible by its unit constant coefficient. Extend it to B_q; uniqueness of localization identifies constant coefficient after extension with the localized stalk map. Thus its kernel maps into the variables ideal (the coefficient criterion at order one). Comap-power monotonicity and the coefficient criterion at order n kill all low-degree coefficients. Translate back through the base stalk isomorphism.

lean.statement:
theorem powerSeries_low_coeff_germ_eq_zero_of_kernel_pow
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (d : ℕ)
    (V : (Spec (.of (MvPowerSeries (Fin d) A))).Opens) :
    let z := Spec.map
      (CommRingCat.ofHom (MvPowerSeries.constantCoeff (σ := Fin d) (R := A)))
    let r := ((ΓSpecIso (.of (MvPowerSeries (Fin d) A))).inv ≫ V.ι.appTop).hom
    ∀ (b : MvPowerSeries (Fin d) A) (n : ℕ) (x : (z ⁻¹ᵁ V).toScheme),
      (V.toScheme.presheaf.Γgerm ((z ∣_ V) x)).hom (r b) ∈
        (RingHom.ker ((z ∣_ V).stalkMap x).hom) ^ n →
      ∀ E : Fin d →₀ ℕ, E.degree < n →
        ((Spec (.of A)).presheaf.Γgerm ((z ⁻¹ᵁ V).ι x)).hom
          ((ΓSpecIso (.of A)).inv.hom (MvPowerSeries.coeff E b)) = 0
